summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (53/52)

data.turoyo: ʕMiro yo, annaqqa lə komʔaṯər mede aʕle."
data.translation: Er ist ja Emir, und auf den macht nichts (auch die größte Summe nicht) Eindruck."

rationale: New active Infectum box; negated impression with target aʕle. Only the supplied verse is quoted, not the reader’s expanded context.

data.turoyo: Omər: "I alayo, d simoli, mʔaṯalla aʕlayye, xd a traktorat du zamanano, d kodawri.
data.translation: Der Pflug, den ich angefertigt hatte, machte auf sie einen solchen Eindruck wie die Traktoren, mit denen man in der heutigen Zeit pflügt.

rationale: Fills active Preterit sense 1; a plough impresses people with ʕal target and feminine agent.

data.turoyo: Hano, u lalyawo azzeyo lu bayto qḥiroyo w lo maḥšamle, ġalabe məhnele ele u xabrano, mʔaṯarle ebe ġalabe. U lalyawo lo daməx hul ṣafro.
data.translation: Der Prinz ging verärgert nach Hause und aß nicht zu Abend. Dieses Wort hatte ihn schwer getroffen. Er schlief die Nacht nicht bis zum Morgen.

rationale: Fills active Preterit sense 1; b-coded affected participant and an independently explicit upsetting remark.

data.turoyo: Ġalabe mʔaṯarno mu mawtano, lo kuḏaʕno: u zlamano bi kire, d ubenowole, ʕuyašwo?
data.translation: Dieser tod hat mich sehr erschüttert. Ich weiß nicht: Lebte der Mann von der Miete, die ich ihm zahlte?

rationale: Fills Detransitive Preterit sense 1; explicit m-coded death stimulus motivates the wider emotional gloss.

data.turoyo: I kačkaṯe ġalabe mʔaṯro ʕal u maktubano d mtaraslela, lu gawro; w mətyaqallale.
data.translation: Die junge Frau wurde sehr traurig über den Brief, den er ihr geschickt hatte, und glaubte ihm.

rationale: Fills Detransitive Preterit sense 1 to five; ʕal-coded letter stimulus and sadness without asserted anger.

after: sich ärgern, betrübt oder erschüttert sein (mit m-; ʕal-)
rationale: The death stimulus at 2/122 and letter at 62/94 show distress without necessary anger; inherited 24/212 and 24/239 already combine sorrow with anger. Broaden the existing emotional gloss rather than split Detransitive sense 2.

summary: Active II.1 describes a stimulus making an impression, with ʕal in 35/45 and 63/224 and b- in 115/42. The remark is the grammatical actor in 115/42, not the affected prince.

Detransitive sense 1 is widened to emotional distress or shock: 2/122 has a death stimulus with m-, and 62/94 has a letter with ʕal-. Existing anger-plus-grief examples support continuity; no new D2 is numbered.

Experiencer coding differs by diathesis: in the Detransitive the affected experiencer has the subject endings, while the cause can be a prepositional phrase; active material has a stimulus actor and prepositional affected participant.
The Arabic-derived verb and ʕal coding suggest contact-compatible lexical and argument patterns, but these verses alone do not date borrowing or prove an independent calque.

JTM 3.2/39 reports lack of physical effect from gunfire. Its surface mi- and impersonal interpretation leave the diathesis unresolved. It is recorded in decisions and questions without publishing a new Detransitive Infectum-wa box.
No light-verb idiom is added: the verb itself carries affective meaning, even when its target is a heart.
Analyze miʔaṯarwo at JTM 3.2/39: active Infectum-wa with an epenthetic vowel, or Detransitive with an impersonal event? Is a non-emotional “have effect” use lexicalized?
Confirm whether 2/122 and 62/94 share the widened emotional sense with the inherited anger/grief examples; the current proposal retains one Detransitive sense.
Does b- in 115/42 differ systematically from ʕal- targets, or are they variants? The translation compresses two affective predicates.

rationale: The German name has lost h after Sc: the supplied 24/239 has Schahrzaman and the Turoyo names Šahrzamān. Preserve the existing vowel diacritic and restore only the missing consonant.
